artists.biography:
The Cure are an English alternative rock band formed in Crawley, West Sussex in 1976. The band has experienced several line-up changes, with frontman, vocalist, guitarist and principal songwriter Robert Smith being the only constant member. The Cure first began releasing music in the late 1970s with its debut album Three Imaginary Boys (1979); this, along with several early singles, placed the band as part of the post-punk and New Wave movements that had sprung up in the wake of the punk rock revolution in the United Kingdom. During the early 1980s, the band's increasingly dark and tormented music helped form the gothic rock genre.

After the release of Pornography (1982), the band's future was uncertain and Smith was keen to move past the gloomy reputation his band had acquired. With the 1982 single "Let's Go to Bed" Smith began to place a pop sensibility into the band's music (as well as a unique stage look). The Cure's popularity increased as the decade wore on, especially in the United States where the songs "Just Like Heaven", "Lovesong" and "Friday I'm in Love" entered the Billboard Hot 100 chart. By the start of the 1990s, The Cure were one of the most popular alternative rock bands in the world. The band is estimated to have sold 27 million albums as of 2004. The Cure have released thirteen studio albums, 10 EPs and over thirty singles during the course of their career. Since 2010, they have been working on a fourteenth studio album.

perplexity.description:
Acoustic Hits is a collection of acoustic reinterpretations recorded by The Cure in 2001, consisting of eighteen songs spanning the band's twenty-five-year history. The album emerged as a companion piece to Greatest Hits, released that same year as the band's contractual obligation to longtime label Fiction Records came to a close. Rather than simply repackaging existing material, The Cure returned to the studio to re-record their most significant tracks using acoustic instrumentation, transforming the sonic character of songs originally crafted in the band's signature gothic rock and new wave styles.

The selection encompasses the band's most recognizable compositions, including "Boys Don't Cry," "A Forest," "Just Like Heaven," "Lullaby," and "Friday I'm in Love," alongside deeper cuts and the two new tracks "Cut Here" and "Just Say Yes" that appeared on Greatest Hits. The acoustic arrangements strip away the layered synthesizers and production techniques that defined The Cure's studio sound, presenting the songs' melodic and compositional foundations in a more intimate setting. All material was newly remastered by Tim Young at Metropolis Mastering specifically for the collection.

Initially released as a bonus disc accompanying certain versions of Greatest Hits, Acoustic Hits remained unavailable on streaming platforms for over two decades before finally becoming accessible on August 9, 2024. The album was given a standalone vinyl release in 2017 as a 180-gram two-LP set, with 3,250 copies pressed as picture discs. While primarily a contractual release rather than a major commercial statement, Acoustic Hits demonstrates the durability of The Cure's songwriting by presenting their catalog through an alternative sonic lens.
